answer: Each identity sails one voyage carrying a walnut batch, and lands it at the jetty. A voyage claim locks a 70-credit bond and pays a 15-credit fee; the jetty log weighs walnut landings against the voyage manifest, and an over-quota or mismatched landing burns the bond. The k-th voyage fee is 15+6(k-1) credits, so the 1,000th identity pays 6,009, and 1,000 fakes pay 3,012,000 plus 70,000 at risk, no pooling. An honest identity pays 85 once, bond refunded after a clean epoch. A rented-landing ring fails: each receipt is key-bound to one voyage and one walnut hash, so reuse burns both bonds.
